podcast.title: A coffee machine for a tea drinker

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: Do you ever buy things you do not need? Guess: what did Sam buy that he never uses?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is shopping. And I have a confession.
[laugh] Go on.
Last week I walked past a shop with a big sign: fifty percent discount on coffee machines. Ten minutes later, I was carrying one home.
A classic impulse buy! Do you even drink coffee at home?
No! I drink tea. The machine is still in its box. It's brand new.
So take it back and ask for a refund.
I tried. But I lost the receipt, and without it, the shop said no.
Oh, Sam. Always keep the receipt! It's the first rule for any consumer.
Lesson learned. What about you? Are you a careful shopper?
Mostly. I love second-hand clothes. There's a little shop near my flat with amazing jackets, and nothing costs more than twenty manats.
Clever. New clothes can cost an arm and a leg.
Exactly. And I always shop around before I buy something big. I check three or four shops and compare prices online.
I should do that. Last year I stood in a queue for two hours to buy a new phone on the first day.
Two hours! Why?
I wanted to be one of the first. And a month later, it was cheaper. Ugh.
Shops know how to make us want things. The music, the lights, "only three left!" — it's all designed to make us spend.
So should we never buy nice things?
No, I think it's OK to splurge on something now and then — if you really love it and you'll really use it.
Like a coffee machine for a tea drinker?
[laugh] Not like that. Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what is the best — or the worst — thing you have ever bought?
Does anybody want a coffee machine? Brand new! See you next time!
Bye for now!
